analyst_view.overall: Feyenoord (5th, 25 points) host Ajax (2nd, 28 points) in De Klassieker on Sunday, and the numbers already add about 39% to cards for the derby. Giovanni van Bronckhorst's Feyenoord are seven games without a win and lost 0-1 at home to Porto on Tuesday, though Ajax coach Míchel said they played very well; they are without defenders St. Juste, Bos, Beelen and Nieuwkoop and Wessels, with Moder doubtful and Smal and Nelson close to returning, none of which the numbers carry (they have no team news for this match). Ajax are unbeaten in five but miss Dolberg, Mokio, Adingra and Tsygankov; Brandt and Gaaei are back from injury but cannot start both Thursday's Conference League game against Thun and Sunday, and 1908.nl and Voetbalzone differ on which one they start, while Ter Stegen is fit and Amrabat likely starts. Feyenoord have two more days of rest than Ajax. Allard Lindhout referees his second Klassieker; the absences on both sides largely cancel out and most have lasted weeks, so I keep every stat where the numbers put it.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals, 1.7 each roughly, and already take a little off Feyenoord (7 goals in their last six) and add to Ajax (18). Feyenoord's back line is without St. Juste, Bos, Beelen and Nieuwkoop, which helps Ajax, but Ajax lack Dolberg, Adingra and Tsygankov and Brandt may not start; most of these absences have lasted weeks and show in recent form already, so I stay at about 3.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners, 6.4 for Feyenoord at home. A Feyenoord side desperate to end its winless run should push forward and Ajax have conceded plenty of corners lately (31 in six), but the numbers already count both, so I stay at about 10.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards and already add about 39% for the derby. Allard Lindhout, 39, was named by the KNVB; the numbers assume an average referee, and I found no card record for him that points either way (his only previous Klassieker was a 2022/23 cup semi-final that was stopped twice for crowd trouble), so I stay at about 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, 16.2 for Feyenoord. Feyenoord have two more days of rest after Tuesday's game against Porto, while Ajax play Thun on Thursday and rotate between the two games, which slightly favours Feyenoord's legs, but their attack has been blunt and the effect is small, so I stay at about 27.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target and already take about 4% off Feyenoord for poor finishing lately and add 6% to Ajax. Nothing in the team news points clearly either way beyond that, so I stay at about 10.2.
